title: Dart's Hall and the visiting big bands
summary: Bands such as Belton's and the Golden Pheasant played Dart's Hall; banjo and tuba carried the sound before microphones.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: And, like, all of the big bands used to come through there. That's another thing that's just coming back.
Like the Golden Pheasant Band out of Florida.
You don't know that one, huh?
No, I don't know that one.
And, Belton's Band, out of Florida. B-e-l-t-o-n.
Now, I don't know about the Sunset Royals.
Belton's band, and the Golden Pheasant band used to come through there. And, I would always be there, you know. I would always know when some big band was --
How big a dance hall would that have been?
It was a small hall, upstairs.
And, what would there be, about seven or eight pieces?
I think about ten or twelve pieces. Something like that.
Very good band, though. Good sounding. Out of Florida,
Well, these Nighthawks -- did they sort of work around Charleston all the time?
Yeah. They would get together and play, you know. They all worked in the daytime, I mean, that wasn't a special thing, you know. They weren't a real recognized band.
You know, just get together, you know. Whenever they'd get a gig they would get together and do it.
But, you weren't ready to play with them?
I -- no, I wasn't really ready. (laugh) I wasn't ready for them.
Well, these -- the Golden Pheasant and the -- they'd have a banjo in the back would they?
Cause you had to have it to sound, didn't you, so the sound would carry?
No. There were no --there weren't any microphones. They had a banjo in the back.
Most of the bands back, you know, in those days -- they had banjos.
